fair_value_reason: P/E leg: ~22.75x on NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of ~$8.47 (0.25 x FY27 $7.86 + 0.75 x FY28 ~$8.67, the adjusted consensus of ~$8.70 less a small fuel/capacity haircut) = ~$193. FCF leg: NTM FCF of ~$11.1B (the ~$11.45B consensus blend less ~3% for factoring reversal risk and fuel, partly offset by the ~$0.7B powder-metal roll-off) / ~1.368B diluted shares = $8.11 at a 4.1% yield = ~$198. At 60/40 that gives ~$194.8, which I round down to $194. That is $2 below my round-1 $196 (fuel and factoring) and ~$1 above the round-2 agent mean of $192.8. The ~1.6% dividend is excluded.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged: all five forecasters now use NTM EPS and NTM FCF, the tariff and AMRAAM errors are gone, and fair values span $187-197 (mean $192.8) with P(>=187) at 0.54-0.575. New checks cut both ways. The 2026 powder-metal cash cost really is ~$0.7B, so it rolls off and supports FCF. H1 cash flow also carried a +$1.5B factoring boost, and $195 jet fuel is forcing US airline capacity cuts. I set fair value at $194 and leave the ladder within ~0.01 of the mean (P>=187 at 0.562), with low confidence and the thesis break at $148. The next tests are Delta (Oct 9) and RTX/GE on Oct 20, then FY27 appropriations after the Nov-3 midterms.
key_drivers: Multiple: ~24.3x NTM today against a 22-23x horizon assumption. Each turn is worth ~$8.5 per share, and this remains the main source of spread among the forecasters.

FCF: consensus is $8.65B for 2026, $10.54B for 2027 and $11.75B for 2028. 2026 absorbs a ~$0.7B powder-metal cash cost that should roll off, but H1-26 cash flow got a +$1.5B y/y boost from factoring tied to OEM deliveries, so the agents' 3-6% haircut to consensus is reasonable.

Commercial aftermarket vs fuel: jet fuel is ~$195/bbl (IATA, week of Sep 18) and US carriers are cutting Q4 and possibly Q1-27 capacity. Delta on Oct 9 and GE/RTX on Oct 20 will show whether that reaches shop-visit demand.

Defense funding: the CR to Dec 11 blocks new munitions multiyears. AMRAAM is a $20.7B ceiling with ~$240M obligated. Full-year FY27 appropriations after the Nov-3 midterms are the next real munitions catalyst.
Iran/Hormuz: the Strait is still effectively closed. A reopening would compress the defense premium and lower fuel, which partly nets out inside RTX.
